title: Tests start git through Apple's slow launcher
what: Every test run (unittest, pytest, the gate's hook tests and the inert probe) starts the real git binary instead of Apple's /usr/bin/git launcher, defined once in tests/tmp_default.py; when the run would not use the launcher (Homebrew git first on PATH) it changes nothing. Tests check the same git version the table names.
why: Owner, 27 Oct small hours: "Почему наши тесты вообще выполняются 10 минут даже с оптимизацией, ускорится ли это вместе со сменой технологии, возьмем максимально возможную - rust, или параллельной обработки будет достаточно, что делает тесты долгими ?". Measured 27 Oct by the test-speed design and its review: the test suite starts git about 29,000 times (23,750 of 29,387 counted in one run come from relay's own code under test, test_queue included); Apple's launcher in front of git adds 8-12 ms per start (30-round interleaved microbench: 11.8 ms through the launcher, 4.1 ms for the real git); Python's own work is about 1.5% of the time, so a rewrite in Rust saves at most 5-10%; pointing tests at the real git is expected to cut git-heavy files by 55-61%, the suite by about 40% and the gate by about 33% (estimate from paired low-load runs). The gate's median since the probe runs beside the main run (26 Oct 19:07) is 938 s. IP chosen by the front (agent-chosen).
failing_case: A gate's library tests on the owner's Mac with /usr/bin/git first on PATH: every git start in a test pays the launcher's 8-12 ms.
pass_cases: The same tests start the real git (a test asserts which binary runs); results and test counts are unchanged; with Homebrew git first on PATH nothing is linked; the gate's library tests drop by at least 25% on an idle Mac.
where: tests/tmp_default.py (the one place every test run gets its environment)
plugins/core/tests (hook tests run by the gate)
